title: Ultra raises $62 million for fast-growing ‘robots as a service’ business, announces tie-up with AI research firm Physical Intelligence
key_facts: Brooklyn-based Ultra announced it raised $62 million in total and is deepening a partnership with Physical Intelligence.
The money came as a $50 million Series A led by Framework Ventures with Y Combinator, and an earlier $12 million seed round led by Y Combinator and Next View.
Ultra leases robots that pack goods for transit to warehouses on a monthly "robots as a service" basis.
According to the company, its robots have packed more than half a million orders.
Customers pay an up-front integration fee and then a monthly fee for hardware and software support.
Ultra builds and installs the robots; Physical Intelligence, valued at $5.6 billion, supplies the AI that lets them learn.
Ultra CEO Jon Miller Schwartz says it has booked significant revenue (not disclosed) and has been able to raise prices.
Schwartz says humanoid-style scaling in warehouses is about five years away.
quote_evidence: On Friday, the Brooklyn-based company announced it had raised $62 million, while also deepening a partnership with the buzzy “robot brains” AI firm Physical Intelligence.
Ultra’s robots, on the other hand, can be found in warehouses across the country and according to the company, the devices have packed more than half a million orders for shipping.
why_it_matters_hint: Robots are being rented to warehouses instead of bought, with a separate AI firm supplying the software brains.
notes: Order count and pricing claims are the company's. The same Fortune newsletter lists other deals, which were ignored.
